chapter: St. Cyr, Dreamland and the OK festival
title: Other musicians named Christian, unrelated to her husband
summary: Allen notes Charlie, Tommy and Buddy Christian in the discography; none are related. She remarks that many musicians came from New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You haven't in recent years? They're here? Yeah. No, I haven't. I haven't made any. Well, I hope that one of these times we'll have a chance to record you performing with a cheer club group. I'm going to see whether whoever would like to be recorded. Alphabetical. It isn't hard. There are several other Christian names here. They aren't related to Mr. Christian, are they? No. No. Of course you remember. I know that. Charlie Christian. Oh, I know that. Yes, I remember him. And Tommy Christian. It was a band that was active in 1927, but from the names I rather suspect... Well, I can't tell. They made Swamp Blues, Phantom Blues. It might have been a colored band. I'm not sure. And Buddy Christian from New Orleans, I believe. But none of these are in any way related.
Uh-huh. Most of them... You know, so many musicians are from New Orleans.
